name: Aurvek Sorrel-Black Pepper Burn
description: An unlicensed street brand produced in small runs out of a South the Gray Zone co-op, using synth-sorrel and real cracked black pepper steeped in the carbonation stage. Distribution is informal and stock is unpredictable.
flavor_profile: Tart, floral sorrel with an aggressive black pepper heat that builds slowly — no sweetness, completely dry
cultural_context: Aurvek has no advertising budget and no official storefront — it moves through a network of informal vendors and community kitchens. The lack of a consistent label is a point of pride. Tier 3 and 4 consumers occasionally seek it out for the underground cachet, which annoys the co-op founders.
story_hooks: The Aurvek co-op is being pressured by a local enforcement arm of Primark Foods to cease production for alleged formula patent infringement — the sorrel-pepper combination is close to a Primark-held compound ID.
A Tier 4 restaurant has started serving Aurvek at Φ18 a glass as a 'heritage beverage experience,' and the co-op founders are furious but legally powerless.
One of the co-op's three founders has quietly accepted a consulting offer from a megacorp and may be feeding proprietary process information — the other two don't know yet.
